channel.title: The Grid Nexus — Gaming Security for Players
channel.description: Account protection, scam awareness, and platform-specific security guidance for players.

item.title: DDoS and IP Leaks: What Streamers Actually Need to Do
item.author: Kim Njuki
item.description: A DDoS attack floods your connection using your real IP, and that IP leaks through P2P games, Discord direct calls, and stream metadata. Here is what genuinely protects you and the Cloudflare misconception to avoid.

item.title: Account Boosting and Trading: The Fastest Way to Get Banned
item.author: Kim Njuki
item.description: Account boosting, account sharing, and account selling all violate platform terms and carry bans — and the "booster" often steals the account outright. Here is what Riot and Valve actually prohibit and why it is not worth it.

item.title: Gaming on Public Wi-Fi: What’s Actually Risky
item.author: Kim Njuki
item.description: Public Wi-Fi exposes you to evil-twin hotspots, packet sniffing, and session hijacking — and HTTPS alone does not hide which sites you visit. Here is the realistic risk picture and the steps that close it.

item.title: In-App Purchase Fraud and the Chargeback That Backfires
item.author: Kim Njuki
item.description: In-app purchase fraud cuts both ways: platforms have been fined for dark-pattern billing, but disputing a charge can also get your account locked. Here is what the FTC found and how to handle an unwanted charge safely.

item.title: Pirated Games and Emulators: The Malware You Download With Them
item.author: Kim Njuki
item.description: Pirated games are one of the most reliable malware delivery channels there is — one campaign alone hit 400,000+ devices. Emulators themselves are usually safe; fake emulator sites are not. Here is what to watch for.

item.title: Buying a Used Console? Check for a Ban First
item.author: Kim Njuki
item.description: Used consoles now carry a risk older hardware never did: the device itself can be banned from online services, and a factory reset will not fix it. Here is what caused it, how to check, and how to protect yourself as a buyer.

item.title: Kernel Anti-Cheat: What It Can See and Why It Worries People
item.author: Kim Njuki
item.description: Kernel-level anti-cheat drivers run with the deepest access Windows allows. Academic research found Vanguard and FACEIT behave in rootkit-like ways, while BattlEye and EAC do not. Here is the actual trade-off, in plain language.

item.title: Roblox for Parents: Locking Down Your Child’s Account
item.author: Kim Njuki
item.description: Roblox’s parental controls live behind a linked parent account with verified age. This walks through linking it, securing the parent login, and setting content maturity, chat, screen time, and spending limits.

item.title: Minecraft Mods and the Malware That Hid Inside Them
item.author: Kim Njuki
item.description: Two major incidents showed that Minecraft mods are a real malware vector: Fracturiser hid in popular CurseForge mods, and BleedingPipe exploited a deserialization bug to run code on servers and players. Here is what both were and how to download mods safely.

item.title: Doxxing and Swatting: What Actually Protects You
item.author: Kim Njuki
item.description: Swatting is a hoax emergency call meant to draw armed police to your home, and doxxing is how attackers find your address in the first place. This covers the FBI’s protective steps, the 911 address flag, and what to do if it happens.

item.title: Passkeys for Gamers: Which Platforms Actually Support Them
item.author: Kim Njuki
item.description: Passkeys are the most phishing-resistant login available, but gaming platform support is uneven. This is the accurate, current picture: Discord, PlayStation, and Xbox support them; Steam and Epic do not. Plus how to set one up where you can.

item.title: SIM Swapping: The Phone-Number Attack That Beats Your Password
item.author: Kim Njuki
item.description: SIM swapping defeats any account that uses SMS for recovery or two-factor. Here is how the attack works, what the 2024 FCC rules require carriers to do, and the concrete steps that stop it from reaching your gaming accounts.

item.title: The Steam Trade That Looks Fine Until Your Skins Are Gone
item.author: Kim Njuki
item.description: The Steam API scam is the most common way CS2 skins get stolen. A phished login creates an API key that watches your trades, cancels the real one, and substitutes a fake. Here is the full mechanism and the checklist that stops it.

item.title: The Fake Cheat That Drains Every Account You Own
item.author: Kim Njuki
item.description: Free cheats and mods are the most reliable way infostealer malware reaches gaming PCs. This explains the RedLine, Vidar, and PirateFi campaigns, what the malware takes, and how to spot a fake before you run it.

item.title: How Your Discord Account Actually Gets Stolen
item.author: Kim Njuki
item.description: Discord accounts get stolen through malware that harvests your login token and through QR-login phishing that tricks you into approving an attacker’s session. Here is how both work and what actually stops them.

item.title: Mobile Gaming Security in East Africa: M-Pesa, APK & SIM-Swap Risks
item.author: Kim Njuki
item.description: How mobile-money scams, SIM-swap attacks and sideloaded APKs put East African gaming accounts at risk — and the concrete steps that stop them.

item.title: Gaming PC Security Hardening Guide: Memory Integrity, VBS, and FPS-safe Windows Settings
item.author: Kim Njuki
item.description: Gaming PC security hardening protects your Windows machine, game accounts, network and drivers without costing you frames. Learn how Memory Integrity affects FPS, which anti-cheat tools require Secure Boot and TPM, and how to lock down Steam, Discord, Battle.net and your router in a 30-minute sprint.

item.title: The Ultimate Mobile Gaming Security Guide: Protect iOS and Android Accounts
item.author: Kim Njuki
item.description: Mobile gaming security is a stack of layers, not a single setting. Learn how to lock down iOS and Android gaming accounts with unique passwords, a password manager, two-factor authentication and passkeys, official app stores, permission reviews, and a monthly session audit — plus the exact steps to take in the first hour if an account is taken over.

item.title: The Ultimate Guide to Steam, Xbox, PlayStation, and Discord Security
item.author: Kim Njuki
item.description: A practical guide to protecting Steam, Xbox, PlayStation, and Discord accounts, covering 2FA, Steam Guard, password hygiene, platform-specific scams, console privacy settings, and Discord server hardening.

item.title: The Ultimate Guide to How to Improve Security for Online Gaming
item.author: Kim Njuki
item.description: A practical guide to online gaming security covering account protection, device hygiene, network safety, and privacy so gamers can play without getting hacked.

item.title: Gaming Security in 2026: How to Actually Keep Your Accounts Safe
item.author: Kim Njuki
item.description: A practical, no-fluff breakdown of the real threats facing gamer accounts in 2026 - credential stuffing, SIM-swap fraud, and malware disguised as mods or skins - plus the concrete steps players, streamers, and platforms should take to lock things down.

item.title: Gaming Router Security Guide: Protect Your Home Network and Your Latency
item.author: Kim Njuki
item.description: Gaming routers have more attack surface than general home routers due to additional management features. This guide covers firmware hygiene, network segmentation, QoS configuration, and common router attack vectors specific to gaming setups.
